tasks.short: Allocate teaching and clinical supervision, handle and decide budget and travel requests, pass approved requests to finance, represent the department, and compile data for accreditation and quality reports.

steps.what: Nursing instructor allocates teaching and clinical supervision tasks as department head
Staff member submits a budget or travel request on the workflow form
Nursing instructor prepares budget and travel requests: from e-mails today, from the workflow form that shows the remaining budget after the change
Nursing instructor checks each budget and travel request and decides: amount, purpose and remaining budget
Nursing instructor releases each approved request to finance: by e-mail today, from the workflow form after the change
Nursing instructor represents the department in faculty meetings
Nursing instructor compiles data for accreditation and quality reports

tasks.design: A teaching-load planner adds up teaching and supervision hours per staff member from the course catalogue and contracts, so overloads show before allocation. Budget and travel requests come in through a workflow form ({WORKFLOW}) that shows the remaining budget; once the head checks and decides, the head releases approved requests to finance from the same form. A quality dashboard ({BI}) shows pass rates, student evaluations and placement figures for accreditation. Representing the department and deciding stay with the head.
tasks.previous_blocker: Loads were added up in spreadsheets, requests came by e-mail and quality figures were gathered by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Load planners, request workflows and quality dashboards are common in universities.
tasks.still_hard: Fair allocation weighs wishes and history no planner knows.
tasks.human_edge: Protecting a colleague's research time in a heavy teaching year.

reach.learn: Whether figures are ready on time.

evidence.claim: Teaching-load planners, request workflows and quality dashboards are common university tools.
Systems able to monitor staff, such as per-staff dashboards, need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the course list to quality figures; faculty budget setting is outside.
Input contract: hours from the catalogue; results from student administration; fallback is spreadsheets and e-mail.
Representing and deciding stay with the head.

Staff submit requests in the form in about the time an e-mail took; their entry is shown in s1b. s1 keeps 60 for deciding the allocation; s2 keeps 50; s4 keeps 20 for the release; s6 keeps 50 for reading and explaining figures.

incremental.description: Nursing instructor checks dashboard figures before accreditation.

approvals.approved_version: Each request with amount, purpose and decision exactly as checked by the head in s3, released once from the form to finance; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the dashboard lacks placement figures, so s6 keeps 75, and staff keep e-mailing requests, so s2 keeps 80 (20.2); high: dashboard and form as assumed (30.8).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Gather each colleague's teaching evaluations, publications and hours, read their self-reflection, hold the evaluation talk, write the evaluation report, sign it with the colleague, and send it to HR.

steps.what: Nursing instructor gathers teaching evaluations, publications and hours for faculty performance evaluations
Nursing instructor reads the colleague's self-reflection
Nursing instructor conducts the evaluation talk
Nursing instructor completes the prefilled report form: hours, evaluation scores, publications and the talk's agenda points
Nursing instructor writes the evaluation of the colleague's performance in the report
Nursing instructor checks the final report with the colleague: the evaluation says what was discussed and the data are right, and both sign it
Nursing instructor files the signed report: by e-mail to HR today, in the HR system after the change

tasks.design: The review form in the HR system ({HCM}) is prefilled with teaching hours, student evaluation scores and publications from the research information system, so the head does not gather them by hand. The prefilled data are a starting point, not a rating. The report form follows the talk's agenda. Once the head and colleague have checked and signed it, the head files the report in the HR system. Reading the reflection, the talk and the judgement stay with the head.
tasks.previous_blocker: Data were gathered from several systems into a spreadsheet and reports were typed and e-mailed.
tasks.enabler_now: HR review forms can be prefilled from teaching and research systems.
tasks.still_hard: Student evaluation scores can be unfair to strict teachers.
tasks.human_edge: Giving hard feedback so the colleague leaves with a plan, not a grudge.

reach.learn: Whether reports are filed on time.

evidence.claim: HR review forms can be prefilled from teaching and research systems.
Systems able to monitor staff performance need works council consent.
A staff decision based solely on automated processing is restricted under GDPR article 22; here the head judges.

assumptions: Boundary: from the review cycle to the report filed; promotion decisions are outside.
Input contract: data from student evaluations and the research information system; fallback is gathering by hand.
Talks and judgements do not change.
Colleagues write their reflection as today.
research_questions: Do reviews finish within the cycle more often?

incremental.description: Nursing instructor checks prefilled data with the colleague.

approvals.approved_version: The evaluation report exactly as checked and signed by the head and the colleague in s6, filed once in the HR system; any change needs a new check and signatures.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the research information system is incomplete for clinical staff, so s1 keeps 70 (16.6); high: prefill as assumed (24.1).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Find funding calls, write the research plan, write standard sections and CVs, build the budget, collect partner letters, check the final proposal with the grants office, and submit it through the funder's portal.

steps.what: Nursing instructor searches for external research funding calls
Nursing instructor writes the research plan of the grant proposal
Nursing instructor writes standard sections and CVs

loop.input: The research plan, the institution's templates for data management and knowledge use, and the applicants' records in the research information system.
loop.output: Draft data management plan, knowledge use section and CVs in the funder's format.
loop.check: Code checks every publication resolves by DOI and matches the research information system, and each section fits the funder's length limits; the applicant checks that each drafted section is true for this project and team, and edits and approves it.
loop.stop: Stops when the checks pass and the applicant approves, or after two failed redrafts the applicant writes the section.
loop.why_not_simpler: Sections must fit each project in prose; templates leave most text to write.

steps.what: Nursing instructor builds the budget in the funder's spreadsheet
Nursing instructor collects letters and signatures from partners by e-mail
Nursing instructor checks the final proposal with the grants office: plan, budget, sections and letters match the call rules
Nursing instructor submits the proposal through the funder's portal

tasks.design: The grants office sends call alerts matched to the department's topics. A bounded step drafts the standard sections and CVs from institutional templates and the research information system; code checks publications and length limits, and the applicant edits. The budget sheet computes staff costs from finance's current rates. Partner letters are requested and signed electronically ({ESIGN}). The research plan is written by the applicant. Once checked with the grants office, the applicant submits the proposal.
tasks.previous_blocker: Standard sections and CVs were rewritten for each call and budgets built by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Research information systems hold publications; language models draft standard text from templates.
tasks.still_hard: Success depends on the idea and the research plan.
tasks.human_edge: Framing a nursing research question so a funder sees why it matters for patients.
tasks.altitude: The applicant writes the plan and edits standard sections instead of rewriting them.

reach.learn: Whether proposals arrive complete before the deadline.

evidence.claim: Language models can draft standard proposal sections from templates, with publications checked against source records.
NWO referees may not use generative AI; uploading a proposal breaches confidentiality.

assumptions: Boundary: from the research idea to the proposal submitted; grant award is outside.
Input contract: templates from the grants office; publications in the research information system; fallback is writing by hand.
The research plan stays the applicant's own text.
Partners sign electronically in about the time a scanned letter took.
s3 keeps 60 because CVs come from records but standard sections still need writing for this project; s4 keeps 60 because rates are filled but planning costs stays; s5 keeps 70 for chasing partners.
research_questions: How much of the drafted sections does the applicant change?

incremental.description: Nursing instructor keeps publication records current.

approvals.approved_version: The proposal with plan, budget, sections and letters exactly as checked with the grants office in s6, submitted once through the funder's portal for this call; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: templates and rates lag behind the call, so s3 and s4 keep 80 (14.0); high: templates and rates current as assumed (21.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Meet the student board, attend events, answer board questions, check activity plans and budgets, forward approved plans to the faculty office, and write board membership certificates.

steps.what: Nursing instructor acts as adviser to the student organization's board
Nursing instructor attends student organization events
Nursing instructor answers board questions on rules and funding by e-mail
Board member submits the activity plan and budget on the form
Nursing instructor checks the form's flags on budget limits and missing fields in activity plans
Nursing instructor judges whether each activity plan and budget fits faculty rules and approves it
Nursing instructor releases the approved plan to the faculty office: by e-mail today, from the form after the change
Nursing instructor writes certificates of board membership

tasks.design: A page for student organisations ({DOCS}) answers common questions on rules, room bookings and funding. Activity plans and budgets come in on a form ({WORKFLOW}) that checks budget limits and required fields, and once the adviser checks and approves, the adviser releases the plan to the faculty office from the form. Certificates use a template. Advising the board and attending events stay with the instructor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Questions, plans and budgets came by e-mail in many formats.
tasks.enabler_now: FAQ pages and forms with field checks are easy to set up.
tasks.still_hard: Boards change every year and start without knowing the rules.
tasks.human_edge: Helping a new board handle a conflict among members.
tasks.altitude: Fewer repeated questions and checks; advising stays.

evidence.claim: FAQ pages and forms with field and limit checks are standard tools.

assumptions: Boundary: from the board agenda to certificates; the organisation's own finances are outside.
Input contract: rules kept by the faculty office; fallback is e-mail.

Board members fill the form in about the time an e-mail took; their entry is shown in s3b. s3 keeps 70; s4 keeps 40 for reading the flags; s6 keeps 20 for the release; s7 keeps 50 for checking names and roles.
Advising and attending do not change.
research_questions: Do plans arrive complete more often?

incremental.description: Nursing instructor updates the page for each new board.

approvals.approved_version: The activity plan and budget exactly as checked and approved by the adviser in s5, released once from the form to the faculty office; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: boards seldom use the page, so s3 keeps 90, and many plans still come by e-mail, so s4 keeps 80 (8.7); high: page and form as assumed (14.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The nursing instructor keeps leading the department, judging colleagues, writing research plans and advising students; spreadsheets, e-mail requests and rewritten standard sections shrink.
role.ambitious_version: An instructor with more time for research and people.
